meta.title: Costco Loses Money On This $1.50 Hot Dog On Purpose. Here's The Real Business.
meta.hook: This hot dog has cost $1.50 since 1985.
meta.description: Costco's hot dog and soda combo has cost $1.50 since 1985, even though inflation pushed that same $1.50 past $4. It isn't charity. In fiscal 2024 Costco collected $4.83 billion in membership fees against $7.37 billion in total net income, meaning roughly two thirds of its profit came from members simply renewing. With a 92.9% US and Canada renewal rate, the $1.50 hot dog is one of the highest-ROI retention tools in American retail.

scenes.narration: This hot dog has cost one dollar fifty since nineteen eighty-five.

visual.query: hot dog in bun close up macro food
visual.visual_intent: Extreme macro of a grilled hot dog in a bun on a plain tray under bright light, steam rising, slow motion, hyper real
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the object itself, hard cut

scenes.narration: Not because Costco can't raise the price. Because raising it would cost them billions.

visual.query: warehouse store aisle pallet racking wide shot
visual.visual_intent: A cavernous warehouse store aisle with towering pallet racks, cool fluorescent light, one point perspective, cinematic
visual.decision_reason: establishes the business behind the price

scenes.narration: Adjusted for inflation, a dollar fifty in nineteen eighty-five is over four dollars today. Costco eats that difference, deliberately.

visual.query: dollar bills cash money burning close up dark
visual.visual_intent: A stack of dollar bills on a dark surface with dramatic side light, smoke curling, slow motion, cinematic
visual.decision_reason: visualises the absorbed inflation cost, BLS CPI verified

scenes.narration: When the CEO told the founder they were losing money on it, the founder's reply was blunt. Raise the hot dog, and I will kill you.

visual.query: two businessmen talking tense boardroom silhouette
visual.visual_intent: Two executives facing each other across a long boardroom table, hard slatted blind shadows, high contrast, cinematic thriller grade
visual.decision_reason: paraphrased quote widely reported by Jelinek, marked as reported

scenes.narration: But here's what nobody talks about. Costco doesn't make its money selling you things.

visual.query: membership card swipe checkout counter close up
visual.visual_intent: A plastic card sliding across a checkout counter into a hand, top down macro, warm retail lighting, slow motion
broll_keywords: credit card payment counter close up
visual.decision_reason: the curiosity gap turn, the card is the real product

scenes.narration: In fiscal twenty twenty-four, membership fees brought in four point eight billion dollars, against seven point four billion in total profit. Roughly two thirds of Costco's profit comes from people just renewing a card.

visual.query: financial data chart bars rising screen dark
visual.visual_intent: Glowing bar columns rising on a dark financial display, one clearly dwarfing the other, minimal cinematic render, teal and gold
visual.decision_reason: exact figures from Costco FY2024 Form 10-K

scenes.narration: The hot dog isn't food. It's a retention tool. And ninety-three percent of US members renew. So Costco didn't raise the price. They built their own hot dog factory instead. Follow for more.

visual.query: food factory production line sausages machinery
visual.visual_intent: An industrial food line with product moving in rows through stainless steel machinery, cold clinical light, overhead tracking, documentary realism
visual.decision_reason: the vertical integration payoff and CTA
